pr_title: fix(router): Only trigger router navigation on `popstate` events from `Location` subscription
pr_body:
With the merging of #41730, our tests now more closely emulate real
browser behavior. This means that we can make changes to the `Router` which depend
on actual browser behavior rather than incorrectly mocked test behavior.

This change updates the logic in the `Router` to only trigger
navigations on `popstate` events. Since our `SpyLocation` now triggers
the `popstate` event correctly on `simulateHashChange`, `back`,
`forward`, and `simulatePopState`, we are able to rely on this being
true for all of these navigations in tests when using `SpyLocation` (the
default for `RouterTestingModule`).

In addition, this behavior relies on documented browser behavior: The
`popstate` event happens due to browser transitions as a result of user
triggered "back" button or otherwise.
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/popstate_event#when_popstate_is_sent

In addition, this change chooses `popstate` over `hashchange` because it
is the event that is already being used for navigations since the
documented behavior of browsers is that `popstate` happens before
`hashchange`.

fixes #41782

reviewer note: this is marked as `major` because #41730 was merged as a breaking change to the `major` branch.

issue_context.title: Changing the URI in the browser directly will fire guards and resolvers of the route TWICE
issue_context.body:
# 🐞 Changing the URI in the browser directly will fire guards and resolvers of the route TWICE ### Affected Package The issue is caused by package @angular/router when using "useHash: true" **FYI / Heads Up:** This issue is reproducible in Firefox based browsers ONLY - so it MAY be a browser bug (emitting the 'popstate' / 'hashchange' events). On the other hand - it may be working in Chromium based browsers because of sheer race-condition luck, I don't know. This issue is reproducible with Waterfox G3.2.1 64-Bit (which is based on Firefox ESR), and the up-to-date (as of this writing) versions of regular Firefox and its Developer Edition. ### Description When changing the URL in the browser's location bar *directly* - by - copy/pasting a link from an email into it - dragging a link from the Angular app into it - or just manually typing it the guards and resolvers of this route will fire TWICE each. **This is especially bad when the resolver is trying to get a LOCK for a mutable resource!!** Weird things happen: While the component to update the resource is about to be created by the Angular router, the second resolve fails (because the resource is locked now) and redirects the user to some kind of resource overview page. **So the lock is now being held by US (unknowingly).** ## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction [https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-11-hashchange-bug](Stackblitz) Please remember the issue only manifests when dragging the link into the URI bar. Clicking the links (and thus opening a new window) works as expected. 👍 ## Demonstration ![ng11-hashchange-bug](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4144388/115863098-4606ba00-a435-11eb-97e5-3195770bcfc7.gif) ### Expectation: 1. the guard will fire (once!) 2. on error the router redirects (once!) 3. on success the routing process continues 4. the resolver will fire (once!) 5. on error the router redirects (once!) 6. on success the lock.component is created and everything is fine ### Outcome: As you can see, the guard and resolver fire twice for a single URI change. The outcome is based on the combination of whether the guard and the resolver are succeeding or not. There are multiple variants, the worst one being the one described above at 'This is especially bad...'. But if the resource was locked (e.g. by a third-party) already - it can result in double error boxes, etc. ### Here is a browser log of a case: ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4144388/115865326-7439c900-a438-11eb-8cb8-90dfccfaab53.png) After the routing to '/redirect-to' just finished (NavigationEnd / Scroll) - just milliseconds later the router is detecting a request to route to '/lock-something' again (with navigationTrigger: "hashchange") and re-starts the navigation (NavigationStart) - including all guards and resolvers of course! 😶 ## 🌍 Your Environment

review_comments: I'd propose adding a comment here to explain why we use 'popstate' or 'hashchange' (why we do not use `event['type']` directly). The way we read `type` and `url` (below) is to avoid Closure optimization issue caused by property renaming? If yes, I think it'd be great to add a quick comment on that too (here and where we read `url` below), so that we don't refactor this code later and accidentally break Router.
